quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 40 Questions • Passing Score 35

questions.question: You should keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you:

options.text: When it will be harder to stop than usual.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.
To prevent the driver in front of you from knowing you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it will be harder to stop than usual.
questions.explanation: You need extra space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. This includes slippery pavement, poor visibility, or heavy traffic. Keep a larger following distance in these situations.

questions.question: How can you make yourself more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride close to vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Ride with your headlight on and position your motorcycle where oncoming traffic can see it best. Keep space between you and other vehicles so you can react to danger. Eye contact alone is not enough to ensure drivers see you.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Hold the handlebars tight and slowly ease off the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars tight and slowly ease off the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when wobbling because it will make it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not use the brakes, as this can also worsen the wobble.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Use only your mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn your head to look for traffic behind you.
Slam on the brakes to let vehicles in your blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to look for traffic behind you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. You must always look over your shoulder before changing lanes to check for traffic you cannot see in your mirrors.

questions.question: Small vehicles can look ______ and seem to travel ______ than they actually do.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, slower
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can appear farther away and seem to move slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge where they are and how fast they are going.

questions.question: The center of a traffic lane is where:

options.text: Debris and oil from cars collect.
Motorcycle riders should always travel for safety.
Drivers are least likely to see a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Debris and oil from cars collect.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane collects debris and oil drippings from cars. You may also find hazards like manhole covers in this area.

questions.question: Drivers entering the highway from an entrance ramp on your right may not see you. You should:

options.text: Move to the left side of your lane so they can merge if needed.
Move to another lane if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane if needed.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of room to vehicles merging onto the highway. Switch to another lane away from the entrance ramp if possible. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to make room for the merging vehicle.

questions.question: Your knees should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Press your knees against the gas tank to help you stay balanced when turning the motorcycle.

questions.question: When a group of motorcycles enters a highway or curve, riders should:

options.text: Ride on the far right of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride single-file.
questions.explanation: While a staggered formation is usually best for group riding, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?
questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should stay just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: What do experienced riders do with their lane position?

options.text: Changes positions within their lane as conditions change.
Stays in one portion of a lane at all times.
Weaves within the lane to be more visible.
Travels only on the oily portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes positions within their lane as conditions change.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders have three lane position options. Choose the safest position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When riding at night, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Allow more space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use your high beam whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tailgate other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, ride slowly and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Be flexible with your lane position when riding at night.

questions.question: When weight transfers to the front of your bike while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Gradually increase pressure to the front brake.
Not worry. The weight transfer will not have an effect on your motorcycle.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually increase pressure to the front brake.
questions.explanation: While braking, slowly increase the pressure on the front brake lever as weight shifts forward to the front tire.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits right turns. Making a right turn at this intersection is unsafe and illegal.

questions.question: Where do most motorcycle and car accidents happen?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle and car collisions happen at intersections. Usually, the car driver fails to give the right-of-way to the motorcycle.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?

options.text: Provides less than half of a motorcycle's braking power.
Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's braking power.
Should not be used unless the roadway is wet.
Should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's braking power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake and provides at least 70 percent of total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what may you need to adjust?
questions.correctAnswerText: The suspension.
questions.explanation: Add a few pounds of pressure to your tires for a passenger. Also adjust the suspension to handle the extra weight.

questions.question: How does riding with a passenger affect your motorcycle?

options.text: Usually results in no difference in handling a motorcycle.
Is usually safe for beginning riders.
Can affect the handling of a motorcycle.
Is encouraged to get operators used to different riding situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect the handling of a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: At night, should your following distance be longer or shorter than during the day?

options.text: Allow a longer following distance at night.
Allow a shorter following distance at night.
Keep the same following distance day or night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distance in the dark. You cannot see shadows or light contrasts as well. Use a longer following distance at night than during the day.

questions.question: Besides watching for bad road conditions, riders should also look for:

options.text: Oncoming traffic that might turn left in front of you.
Traffic entering from side roads on both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Scan ahead, to the sides, and behind your motorcycle at all times. Look for bad road conditions and traffic that could be dangerous.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
Move between the three portions of the lane as they pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases your chance of a crash. Riding on the far side may make the other driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When slowing down or stopping, you should use both brakes:
questions.correctAnswerText: Every time.
questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the strongest stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding with other motorcyclists in a staggered formation, when should you NOT use it?

options.text: It should not be used at any time.
Do not use it when entering or leaving a highway.
Do not use it when riding through curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use it when entering or leaving a highway.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually good. However, switch to single-file when riding through curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, how should you sit?

options.text: Sit in your normal comfortable position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit in your normal comfortable position.
questions.explanation: Have a seat large enough for both you and your passenger without crowding. Do not sit any farther forward than you normally do.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: The rear brake is operated with your right foot.

questions.question: A small animal enters your lane while you are in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Swerve into another lane to avoid the animal.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal if you can do so safely. In traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane could cause you to crash with another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another car.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic.
Ignore the stop line and move forward to look.
Stop at the stop line and then proceed through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Stop where indicated at the stop line. Then move forward and stop again just before the crossing traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader, toward the front of the group. This lets more experienced riders watch them without making the inexperienced rider lead the group.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do?

options.text: Spread out to make the group easier to see.
Stay close together to make the group easier to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
questions.explanation: Riders should stay close together in a group. This makes the group easier to see and keeps riders from getting separated. Each rider needs enough space to maneuver safely. Riding in pairs does not give riders enough room to move around.

questions.question: The body gets rid of about one drink per hour. A person drinks 7 drinks in 3 hours. How many drinks will likely be in their system 3 hours after their last drink?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours since the last drink from the total drinks consumed. A person who had 7 drinks in 3 hours will have about 4 drinks left in their system 3 hours later.

questions.question: Another vehicle is following you too closely. What should you do?

options.text: Allow the other driver to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the other driver to pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. Change lanes safely and let them go ahead. Speeding up will only increase danger and encourage them to tailgate at higher speeds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the marked line. If there is no line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop at a point where you can see oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this warning sign tell drivers about?
questions.correctAnswerText: Road curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to what is just ahead. This sign warns drivers about an upcoming right curve.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: To tell other motorists that you are riding near them.
To help other motorists see your motorcycle in slow traffic.
To warn other motorists that you are slowing down or stopping where they do not expect it.

questions.correctAnswerText: To warn other motorists that you are slowing down or stopping where they do not expect it.
questions.explanation: Use your brake light to communicate with other drivers. Flash your brake light before slowing for a sharp turn or when slowing in any place where drivers may not expect it.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closer to the passing driver increases the risk of a crash. Riding on the far side might make them return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway begins.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead is now divided. Stay to the right of the divider or median.

questions.question: What should a face shield do?

options.text: Allow a clear view to both sides.
Prevent air from passing through it.
Be tight enough to prevent glasses from fitting underneath it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a clear view to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield must be free of scratches, resist damage, allow clear views to both sides, fasten securely, permit air to pass through, and have room for eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: Where do motorcycles face the greatest risk of conflict with other traffic?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are the most dangerous places for motorcycle conflicts with other vehicles. Stay alert at intersections where another vehicle may cross into your path.
